messages:
customer-ops: Hey team — onboarding a customer in a locked-down VPC. Private installer fails at bootstrap: can't pull model blobs, telemetry callouts time out, and we see a 403 from the registry. Can we get a minimal outbound list so they can run the installer?

jeni_support: Thanks — can you paste the installer logs and a quick repro `curl -Iv` against the registry? often this is DNS/SNI or proxy rewriting.

customer-ops: Pasting trimmed curl from their VM (they're in a NATed subnet):

```
$ curl -Iv https://registry.redwood-inference.net/models/abc123
*   Trying 34.201.12.34:443... connected
* TLS handshake has read 1024 bytes and written 1032 bytes
* SSL: certificate subject name mismatch
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name mismatch
```

customer-ops: Also another vm shows `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known` when hitting telemetry, so DNS sometimes fails.

jeni_support: The cert mismatch + intermittent DNS smells like a corporate TLS-intercept or split-horizon DNS. Two common fixes: allow direct egress to our FQDNs (TLS passthrough) or route through a proxy with `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` set for the installer. Which can you do?

sam_sre: Here's a practical minimal FQDN allowlist we ask for during private installs (TCP 443, and 80 for redirects). Please note CDNs and S3 have dynamic IPs; prefer FQDN allowlist or proxy TLS passthrough: 

- registry.redwood-inference.net
- packages.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.redwood-inference.net (model tarballs / shard index)
- telemetry.redwood.ai (v2)
- auth.redwood.ai (token exchange)
- cdn.redwood-inference.net (static assets)
- *.s3.amazonaws.com (model shards)
- d2xx9y2s3g5.cloudfront.net (CDN edge examples)
- ocsp.digicert.com (OCSP checks)
- crl3.digicert.com (CRL)

Also allow outbound NTP/time sync (UDP 123) or make sure the VMs have correct time — TLS can fail if clock skew is large. If they have IPv6 enabled, allow IPv6 443 egress too (we see failures when IPv6 is blocked).

jeni_support: Quick repro commands to run after rules are applied: 

```
# DNS + TLS check
curl -Iv https://registry.redwood-inference.net
# Bypass local DNS to test SNI/cert
curl --resolve registry.redwood-inference.net:443:34.201.12.34 -Iv https://registry.redwood-inference.net
# Package pull test
python3 -m pip download --no-deps -d /tmp/pkgs "requests"
```

infra-bot: Checklist added to thread: allow FQDNs, allow OCSP/CRL, enable TLS passthrough for installer or configure HTTPS_PROXY in systemd unit, ensure NTP, consider DNS forwarding to an external resolver.

customer-ops: One question — customer asked for single CIDR block to whitehole firewall rules. Any stable IP ranges?

sam_sre: Short answer: not for CDN / S3. For control-plane hosts (auth / registry) we can provide ASNs/IP ranges on request but they can change. Recommend FQDN allowlist or using a corporate proxy that supports TLS passthrough. If they must use CIDR, use cloud provider IP ranges for the region + expect occasional changes.

customer-ops: Got it. I'll ask them to open those FQDNs + OCSP and enable NTP. I'll try the `--resolve` step to verify TLS passthrough. Will report back.

(3h later)

customer-ops: Update — customer whitelisted the hostnames and OCSP endpoints, enabled NTP, and the installer completed successfully. Model pulls and telemetry now working. Thanks :tada:

jeni_support: Awesome, thanks for the update — closing the loop. If they want a cron-friendly doc for proxy env vars and systemd snippets I can share one.
